subject.title: feat(slack): Support Slack RTS (Real-Time Search) API via assistant action tokens

question: Should OpenClaw add Slack RTS as a separate assistant action-token search path, and what token containment, privacy, scope, and read-target rules should it use?
rationale: The feature is valid but security-sensitive because it handles event-scoped Slack action tokens and workspace search results, and the closed related PRs used a different user-token `search.messages` API with unresolved authorization concerns.

options.title: Approve narrow RTS contract
options.body: Implement `assistant.search.context` inside the Slack plugin with event-scoped token containment, read-target/privacy rules, redaction, docs, tests, and live Slack proof.

options.title: Consolidate Slack search first
options.body: Define one Slack search product contract covering RTS and any user-token search before accepting implementation work.

options.title: Defer workspace search
options.body: Keep Slack workspace search out until maintainers are ready to own the token, privacy, and validation burden.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow RTS contract
recommendation.body: Implement `assistant.search.context` inside the Slack plugin with event-scoped token containment, read-target/privacy rules, redaction, docs, tests, and live Slack proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This contributor has the strongest recent history across Slack assistant lifecycle, setup, action runtime, and the closed action-parity discussion that routes search back here.
